title: Convective scale nowcasting for Thunderstorms, Hail & Cloudbursts (06 hr)
department: National Centre for Medium Range Weather Forecasting (NCMRWF)
description:
Convective storms, such as severe thunderstorms, hail, downburst winds, and cloudbursts are among India’s deadliest natural hazards, especially during the pre-monsoon and monsoon seasons.Despite advancements in Numerical Weather Prediction (NWP) models, traditional systems often fail to accurately capture these mesoscale extreme weather events.The primary limitation stems from spatial and temporal constraints: these violent storms develop rapidly within a window of minutes and occur at localized scales that slip through coarse grid resolutions. Current early warning infrastructures struggle to provide high-resolution, short-term forecasts (0–6 hours), leaving local administrations, aviation sectors, and rural farming communities vulnerable to sudden, devastating impacts.
The challenge is to build a real-time, convective-scale Nowcasting System (0–6 hour lead time) operating at a hyper-local 1–3 km spatial resolution.
Because traditional physics-based models are too computationally slow to simulate these rapid developments in real-time, participants must design a system rooted in Multi-Source Data Fusion architectures. The core objective is to ingest high-frequency, heterogeneous meteorological streams, automatically detect early convective initiation, and dynamically forecast severe storm parameters (including lightning strike density, hail probability, downburst velocity, and cloudburst thresholds).Design a robust, real-time ingestion engine that fuses data streams from multiple sources: Doppler Weather Radars (DWR - reflectivity and velocity fields), geostationary satellite imagery (INSAT-3D/3DR thermal/infrared bands), and ground-based lightning detection networks. A real-time,interactive GIS-mapped dashboard showcasing high-resolution (1–3 km) hazard zones with live countdown clocks for storm arrivals.
summary: Innovation (4/5): draws on satellite, gis applied to a disaster management problem, placing it in the breakthrough band. Feasibility (3/5): as a software build with moderate integration complexity, a full build is tight for 36 hours and will need scope-cutting. Impact (4/5): addresses a more targeted user group within Disaster Management. Tech Depth (4/5): centers on gis, real-time. Sustainability (3/5): will need a maintenance/upkeep plan post-hackathon. Scalability (2/5): currently scoped narrowly and would need rework to scale. Total 20/30 -> Yellow verdict.

detail.title: Convective-Scale Nowcasting for Thunderstorms, Hail & Cloudbursts (0-6 hr)

overview.in_plain_terms: Build a real-time system predicting severe thunderstorms, hail, and cloudbursts 0-6 hours ahead at a hyper-local 1-3 km resolution, catching these fast, violent storms that slip through the coarser grids of standard weather models.
overview.why_it_matters: These storms develop within minutes and hit hard, aviation, farmers, and local administrations all need genuine short-lead-time warning to actually respond in time.
pain_points: Convective storms develop within minutes at scales too small for coarse NWP grids to capture.
Current early warning infrastructure struggles with high-resolution, short-term (0-6 hour) forecasts.
Traditional physics-based models are too computationally slow for real-time nowcasting at this scale.
overview.background: India's deadliest weather hazards during pre-monsoon and monsoon seasons, severe thunderstorms, hail, and cloudbursts, develop rapidly at localized scales that current NWP infrastructure can't capture in time.
overview.whats_being_asked: A real-time, hyper-local (1-3 km resolution) convective-scale nowcasting system with 0-6 hour lead time, using multi-source data fusion rather than slow physics-based simulation.
expected_solution: Multi-source, high-frequency data fusion architecture (radar, satellite, lightning, model data).
0-6 hour actionable lead time for thunderstorms, hail, and cloudbursts.
Real-time operational capability suitable for aviation and rural warning use.

analysis.innovation_scope_note: Breakthrough. Genuine convective-scale, multi-source nowcasting at this resolution and lead time is active meteorological AI research territory, similar in ambition to SIH26077 and 26078 in this batch.
analysis.invention_effort_note: High. Real-time multi-source data fusion at hyper-local resolution requires substantial data engineering and modeling depth.

competitive_landscape.note: Sits alongside several similarly ambitious MoES nowcasting PS in this batch, differentiation depends on the specific hazard focus (hail specifically is less commonly modeled than general thunderstorm/rainfall nowcasting).

innovation.note: Multi-hazard (thunderstorm, hail, cloudburst) hyper-local nowcasting via data fusion is genuine advanced meteorological ML territory.

invention.note: Multi-source data fusion at 1-3 km resolution with real-time constraints is substantial technical depth.

technical_feasibility.note: Public radar/satellite/lightning data exists but achieving genuine hyper-local resolution and real validated lead time in 36 hours is ambitious.

impact_and_benefits.note: Directly addresses some of India's deadliest weather hazards with clear aviation, agriculture, and public safety relevance.

architecture.note: Multi-source real-time data fusion architecture, genuine architectural sophistication.

overall_verdict.reasoning: Yellow, similar profile to the other nowcasting-focused MoES PS in this batch, genuinely valuable and technically substantial but full operational-grade validation in 36 hours is ambitious. Scope validation to a small set of well-documented historical convective events.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: Explicitly names hail as a distinct hazard type, less commonly addressed than general thunderstorm/rainfall nowcasting, giving a genuine differentiation opportunity if built well.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: Attempting all three hazard types (thunderstorm, hail, cloudburst) simultaneously at full hyper-local resolution and validated lead time will be too broad, scope to 1-2 hazard types built genuinely well.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Consider focusing specifically on hail detection/prediction as your primary differentiator, since it's explicitly named but less commonly the focus of nowcasting PS, while treating the other hazards as secondary or future extensions.

idea_0_4: Choose your primary hazard focus (hail is a strong differentiation choice, or general severe thunderstorm), scope to 1-2 hazard types rather than all three fully.
Source public radar, satellite, and lightning data for a known historical convective event in your test region.
Split: one person on the multi-source data fusion pipeline, one on the nowcasting prediction model.
prototype_4_22: Build your multi-source data fusion pipeline aligning radar, satellite, and lightning data for your test event.
Build your nowcasting model for your chosen primary hazard focus.
Start testing against your historical event's actual documented occurrence and timing.
integration_22_30: Validate your lead time and accuracy against the real historical event.
Test at your target 1-3 km resolution where your data sources support it.
polish_30_36: Build a clear visualization showing your nowcast against real historical event progression at your target resolution.
Rehearse presenting your honest validation results including your actual achieved lead time.
Prepare to discuss extending to the other named hazard types beyond your primary focus.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: If focusing on hail specifically, show your system detecting hail-favorable conditions in advance for a real historical hail event, that specific, less-commonly-addressed hazard focus is a genuine differentiator among the many nowcasting PS in this batch.

strengths: Hail-specific focus offers genuine differentiation from more commonly-addressed thunderstorm/rainfall nowcasting.
Public multi-source data exists for real training and validation.
weaknesses: Attempting all three named hazard types fully at hyper-local resolution isn't achievable in 36 hours.
Sits among several similarly ambitious nowcasting PS in this batch, needs a clear differentiator.

team_fit.ideal_ratio: ML/data-fusion-heavy, with genuine meteorological grounding for hazard-specific feature engineering.
team_fit.approach: Choose your hazard focus and test event early, this concrete validation target shapes the entire build.

ai_buildability_split.ai_can_build_fast: Standard nowcasting model scaffolding and multi-source data pipeline infrastructure.
ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: Identifying which atmospheric signatures specifically precede your chosen hazard type (hail formation signatures differ from general thunderstorm precursors), that requires genuine domain knowledge.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: A generic severe-weather nowcaster without hazard-specific feature engineering would likely underperform on the specific, less-commonly-modeled hazard type (hail) that offers this PS's real differentiation opportunity.

data_resource_availability.status: Public radar, satellite, and lightning network data genuinely exist for many regions and known historical convective events.
data_resource_availability.backup_plan: Not needed, real data access is achievable, though selecting a well-documented historical event for your chosen hazard focus maximizes validation credibility.

judge_qna.question: Why focus on this specific hazard type, and how does your approach differ for hail versus general thunderstorm nowcasting?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Explain the specific atmospheric signatures relevant to your chosen hazard (hail formation requires specific updraft/freezing-level conditions distinct from general convective initiation), showing genuine domain understanding, not a generic severe-weather model applied uniformly.
judge_qna.follow_up: What's your model's actual validated accuracy specifically for this hazard type, not general severe weather?

judge_qna.question: What's your achieved spatial resolution and lead time against real historical data?
judge_qna.strong_answer: State your actual measured resolution and lead time from validation against your real historical test event, honest numbers, not the PS's aspirational target restated as an achievement.
judge_qna.follow_up: What data source limitation is the biggest constraint on further improving resolution or lead time?
